RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Member: Taylor Ellison
Member ID: W423241591
Reference Number: POC-C4BC2EBAC7-30163
Date of Notice: 2026-08-14
Requested Service/CPT: Shoulder labral/instability repair, CPT 29806
Treating Surgeon: Marchetti, MD, Orthopedic Surgery

To the Appeals Review Committee:

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for arthroscopic shoulder capsulorrhaphy/labral repair (CPT 29806), as set forth in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-14 (Reference No. POC-C4BC2EBAC7-30163). This appeal is submitted within the 180-day deadline stated in that notice (by 2027-02-10).

1. Stated reason for denial

The notice states that the request was denied because "the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery." I respectfully disagree and ask that the determination be reversed based on the clinical record summarized below and on the medical-necessity criteria that PacificSource itself has identified as applicable to this procedure.

2. Applicable criteria

PacificSource's public "Clinical Policies and Practice Guidelines" page identifies the Carelon Medical Benefits Management Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines as the adopted external criteria used for Commercial and Medicare musculoskeletal medical-necessity determinations. Within Carelon's Musculoskeletal Appropriate Use Criteria: Joint Surgery guideline (Shoulder Arthroscopy and Open Procedures section, Doc ID MSK02-1125.1, effective 11/15/2025), the criteria located for capsulorrhaphy state, in relevant part:

"Capsulorrhaphy is considered medically necessary when ALL the following criteria are met: History of a shoulder dislocation or recurrent subluxation ... Physical exam consistent with symptomatic glenohumeral instability (e.g., apprehension, relocation, load and shift) ... Failure of at least 12 weeks of conservative management (unless history of traumatic dislocation and multiple dislocations during management)*"

I was not provided the complete verbatim policy excerpt used by the reviewer, and I have not independently confirmed every line of this guideline word-for-word beyond what is quoted above. I therefore also request, under Item 6 below, that PacificSource furnish the specific guideline, section, and version actually relied upon for this denial.

3. How the record meets (and, under the guideline's own exception, exceeds) the conservative-treatment requirement

a. History of dislocation/recurrent subluxation: I have had three anterior shoulder dislocations since symptom onset approximately nine months ago, the most recent of which required reduction in the emergency department. This satisfies the "history of a shoulder dislocation or recurrent subluxation" element quoted above.

b. Functional impact / interference with activities: My instability prevents overhead reaching and lifting required for my job, and I have been unable to return to work in my prior capacity.

c. Physical exam findings: Exam performed by Dr. Marchetti documented positive apprehension and relocation tests and increased anterior translation on load-and-shift testing — precisely the findings referenced in the quoted criterion ("apprehension, relocation, load and shift").

d. Conservative management: I completed 16 weeks (2026-04-01 through 2026-07-22) of supervised physical therapy directed at rotator cuff and scapular stabilizer strengthening with activity modification, totaling 18 visits, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note. This alone exceeds the "at least 12 weeks of conservative management" threshold quoted above. In addition, I used NSAIDs for four months during symptomatic flares. An injection was not administered because, as documented in the record, injections are not indicated for instability.

e. Exception for traumatic, recurrent dislocation: The same guideline criterion quoted above states that the 12-week conservative-management requirement applies "unless history of traumatic dislocation and multiple dislocations during management." My record documents a traumatic dislocation mechanism with three separate anterior dislocation events, including one occurring during the course of conservative management, which independently supports medical necessity under this exception even apart from the 16 weeks of completed therapy.

f. Imaging correlation: MR arthrogram of the shoulder dated 2026-06-03 demonstrates an anteroinferior labral tear (Bankart lesion) with a small Hill-Sachs lesion and glenoid bone loss under 10%, with an intact rotator cuff — findings that clinically correlate with, and explain, the exam findings and instability episodes described above.

g. No contraindications: There is no active infection, no untreated substance use, and I am a non-smoker (BMI 29), so none of the guideline's noted risk or exclusion factors are present.

4. Conclusion

The record — 16 weeks/18 visits of supervised physical therapy, 4 months of NSAID use, three documented anterior dislocations (one requiring ED reduction), positive apprehension/relocation/load-and-shift findings, and MR arthrogram–confirmed Bankart lesion with Hill-Sachs lesion — demonstrates both (a) a completed conservative treatment trial that meets or exceeds the 12-week threshold referenced in the applicable guideline, and (b) qualification under that same guideline's exception for traumatic, recurrent dislocation. I ask that PacificSource reverse the denial and authorize CPT 29806 as requested by Dr. Marchetti.

5. Enclosures

- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-04-01 to 2026-07-22, 18 visits)
- MR arthrogram report, 2026-06-03
- Emergency department reduction record
- Office notes documenting exam findings (apprehension, relocation, load-and-shift) and dislocation history
- Letter of medical necessity from Marchetti, MD
- [Any additional records the provider's office includes]

6. Request for the specific policy relied upon

Because the denial notice did not cite a specific policy title, number, or section, I also request that PacificSource identify and provide, in writing, the complete and exact medical-necessity criteria and policy document (including title, policy/document number, and effective date) that the reviewer applied to this request, so that I and my surgeon may respond to any additional specific requirement not addressed above.

7. Request

I ask that this appeal be reviewed by a physician reviewer with appropriate orthopedic/sports-medicine expertise, and that PacificSource issue a written decision within the timeframe required for internal appeals of pre-service requests. If the internal appeal is not resolved in my favor, I reserve my right to request an external review through the Oregon Division of Financial Regulation's Independent Review Organization process.

Please contact me at [phone number] or [email address] if additional information is needed. Thank you for your prompt attention to this appeal.

Sincerely,

Taylor Ellison
